name: Best Hardware (2026 name)
also_known_as: Best Hardware Project / Best Hardware Special Award (2016 to 2019 results pages use both forms)
file_note: This is a precedents file, not a winners file. The four projects below were chosen for how well they document an instrument like ours, not for having won a prize. None of them won Best Hardware. `verified` means the page was rendered from the live URL and read, and that any award or section claim in `note` was checked against the iGEM results page named there. Best Hardware winners for 2023 to 2025 are covered separately in research/hardware.* by a sibling agent; these four are deliberately outside that set.
ballot: Does the hardware you developed address a need or problem in synthetic biology?
Did the team conduct user testing and learn from user feedback?
Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?
Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

winners.note: Photometer precedent 1. The OD/F Device: a 3D-printed cuvette holder in a laser-cut acrylic case, a 600 nm LED and a TSL235R-LF light-to-frequency sensor, measuring OD600 and GFP fluorescence in one body for a stated $60. Chosen because it is the most completely reproducible DIY photometer write-up in iGEM: a costed bill of materials with supplier links in both euros and dollars, downloadable STL and SVG and Arduino sketches, a twelve-step photographic construction manual, a two-stage calibration onto a lab photospectrometer with its regression coefficients given, and a prior-art paragraph that names what earlier DIY turbidity meters failed to document. It is also the ancestor of the Tsinghua-A device below and of Aachen's own 2015 in-line OD unit, so it is the one page in this bank with a traceable reuse record. Track not confirmed: the 2014 results page would not render (59 words returned), so no section claim is made. Work is spread over three pages, all rendered: the project page, Notebook/Engineering/ODF (the technical detail, BOM and construction manual) and Interlab_Study/Hardware (the parts list and sensor-linearity argument).

Photometer precedent 2. A handheld $20 OD600-and-fluorescence reader for field allergy testing, built around a Beetle (Arduino Leonardo) MCU, two TSL235R sensors behind photographic filter paper, and a 3D-printed cuvette brace with a vibration motor to stop cells settling. Chosen for its validation section, which is the tightest in the bank: a dilution series read on both the device and a spectrophotometer, reported as a fitted equation with its residual distribution (ep ~ N(0, 0.0052)), and the same treatment applied again to the fluorescence channel. Also chosen because it opens by crediting Aachen 2014 and saying in one sentence what it changed, which is the reuse move our pages never make. Short: about 1,400 words. Track not confirmed: the 2018 results page lists the medal sections as a combined 'underover' group, so Tsinghua-A's section cannot be read off it; the same page does confirm Tsinghua-A took a Gold medal (https://2018.igem.org/Competition/Results).

Bioreactor precedent 1. A three-flask continuous-culture reactor for selecting phage variants: Raspberry Pi control, peristaltic pumps, Peltier water baths under PID temperature control, and a self-built in-line OD sensor on a modified flow-through cuvette. The closest architectural match to BR-01 in this bank, and the best failure-narration anywhere in it: its Improvements section tells each design mistake as symptom, investigated cause, and the fix with the part number and the spec that changed. CAD, firmware and model are in one GitHub repository. Track confirmed OG from the 2019 results page, which lists ETH Zurich as an Overgrad Best Hardware nominee and not a winner (https://2019.igem.org/Results2); the same page lists it as an Overgrad Best New Application Project nominee, and the 2018 results page lists it as an Overgrad Best Hardware nominee too. It won neither, which is exactly why it is here.

Bioreactor precedent 2. The openPBR: an open-source flat-panel photobioreactor and turbidostat for Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, nine vessels or three flat panels, 15 to 30 mm path, 95 to 190 mL, with an OPT101 sensor rail reading online optical density against 680 nm LEDs. Chosen for the two things our pages are weakest on: a costed bill of materials broken down by subsystem to a 588 EUR total with a stated reason for publishing it, and a GitHub project that holds assembly instructions, parts list and software together. Its OD section is also the one page here that reports a calibration, then a separate validation on fresh samples against an ideal-correlation line, then the range over which it stops being trustworthy. Track confirmed OG from the 2019 results page, which lists Humboldt Berlin as the Overgrad winner of Best Plant Synthetic Biology (https://2019.igem.org/Results); it was not a Best Hardware winner or nominee.
